problem:
A curve is defined by the parametric equations

$$
x={t}^{2}-8t,\,y=2{t}^{3}.
$$

Determine the value of the parameter $t$ at which the normal line to the curve is horizontal. Do not round the answer.

The normal to the curve is horizontal at $t=$
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
The normal line is horizontal when the tangent line to the curve is vertical. Therefore, we require ${x}^{′}(t)=0$ while ${y}^{′}(t)\ne 0.$

So, we first find the derivatives of $x$ and $y:$

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=2t-8,\,{y}^{′}(t)=6{t}^{2}
$$

Solving ${x}^{′}(t)=0$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2t-8 & =0 \\ 2t & =8 \\ t & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we note that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(4) & =6{(4)}^{2}=96\ne 0,\end{aligned}
$$

which confirms that the normal to the curve is indeed horizontal when $t=4.$
